test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is the maximum time limit for completing the trial of a case under the POCSO Act?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, trials of cases involving child sexual abuse must be completed **within one year** from the date of cognizance by the court.
 
• The time limit aims to ensure speedy justice to the victims of child abuse and prevent prolonged trauma.
 
• This provision is mandated under **Section 35** of the POCSO Act, 2012, which emphasizes the importance of expediting child-related cases.
 
• The Act requires that all proceedings, including evidence collection and judgment, are conducted in a **child-friendly manner** to minimize distress for the victim.
 
• The one-year time frame is part of broader measures introduced to strengthen the judicial framework for protecting children’s rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012:**

 
 
• The POCSO Act was enacted to address the issue of sexual exploitation and abuse of children and provides safeguards for children at every stage of the judicial process.
 
• It defines a "child" as any person below the age of 18 years.
 
• The Act is gender-neutral and applies to offenses committed against both boys and girls.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to the POCSO Act:**
 
 
• The POCSO Act was amended in 2019 to include stricter punishments, including the death penalty, for sexual offenses against children.
 
• The amendment also aimed at ensuring faster trials and reducing delays in delivering justice.
 
 
 
• **Special Courts under POCSO:**
 
 
• The Act mandates the establishment of Special Courts to exclusively handle POCSO cases to ensure a child-sensitive judicial process.
 
• These courts are equipped with trained professionals to handle child witnesses and evidence collection.
 
 
 
• **Child-friendly Procedures:**
 
 
• POCSO emphasizes that the statement of the child victim should be recorded at their residence or a place of their choice in the presence of a trusted adult.
 
• Cross-examinations are conducted in-camera to prevent further trauma to the child.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Obligations:**
 
 
• The Act makes it mandatory for any person with knowledge of a child being sexually abused to report the incident to the police.
 
• Failure to report such cases can lead to penalties under the Act.
